---
title: "Fixed quantile tiers"
subtitle: "3.1 · a simulated league, after the postrank theory book, ch. 9, 16 and 17"
description: "Posterior evaluation of directions stated by quantile groups of the estimates."
---

A quantile-tier rule sorts estimates into groups of nearly equal size. Interpreted as an ordered grade report, it
states every direction between tiers and withholds every comparison within a tier. The grouping uses the estimates
alone; a separately specified posterior evaluates the expected errors of its statements. The display records grade
sizes, disclosure and reporting risk, together with individual errors above the withholding cost. A shared tier
withholds a comparison. Neither membership in a tier nor its size determines the posterior probability that a
particular stated direction is correct.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Three tiers.** Three groups of 10 state 300 of 435 pairs, a share of .690. Under the teaching posterior they
  expect 51.86 wrong directions, .173 per stated direction, and risk .1813 at τ .20. The marks identify all stated pairs with error above τ, including comparisons across several boundaries.
- **Ten tiers, marks on.** Disclosure rises to 405 pairs (.931), but expected wrong directions rise to 89.40 and
  E/N to .221. There are 197 marked pairs; the largest stated error is .802. Risk .2193 exceeds the all-withheld
  report's .2000 at this τ. This comparison does not make τ an error bound for the tier rule.
- **Four tiers.** Quantile positions produce sizes 8, 7, 8, 7 and state 337 pairs (.775). The grouped formula counts within-tier withheld pairs. The equal-size closed form disappears because four does not divide thirty.
- **Two tiers.** Groups of 15 state 225 pairs (.517). Each within-tier triangle holds comparisons the report
  leaves unsaid; arrows read every cell of the pair map.
- **Thirty tiers.** Every pair is stated. The tiers follow the estimates, so their 102.2 expected wrong directions
  differ from the 94.48 of the posterior-mean ranking in [Ranking states many claims](../uncertainty/ranking-claims.qmd).
  With G set to one, E/N becomes “NA: no disclosure,” while risk is .2000.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
These are thirty simulated units in one frozen draw, with independent normal teaching posteriors (prior mean 0,
SD .15). Tier membership is fixed by the grouping rule. τ changes their evaluation and the marked errors, while their membership
stays fixed. The loss evaluates stated directions rather than the purpose a tier rule was designed for. Sizes alone
do not determine how many directions are wrong. Quantile sizes are nearly balanced when estimates have no ties;
the package merges tiers crossed by equal scores.
:::

Standalone: [embed/fixed-tiers.html](../../embed/fixed-tiers.html), for example `?preset=ten-tiers&theme=dark`.
